rows.Potential signal: Rolling offense and defense performance; separate pass/rush and home/away context. Normalize for opponent and game situation before claiming predictive value.
rows.Required observations: Dated team-level game stats, game identifiers, opponent, score, possessions/context and as-of timestamp.
rows.Target / test: Forecast spread and total probabilities; chronological walk-forward test against a frozen market baseline.
rows.Known risk / control: Small samples, opponent strength, garbage-time effects and changing personnel. Avoid same-game outcome leakage; compare simple baseline first.

rows.Potential signal: Starting QB confirmation and historical team/player performance may matter; do not map questionable status directly to a numeric adjustment without evidence.
rows.Required observations: Official report snapshots, confirmed starter, role, game stats and prices captured at the same decision time.
rows.Target / test: Test incremental log-loss / calibration change versus a model without status feature, within out-of-sample periods.
rows.Known risk / control: Report status is not a probability of playing. Status changes are time-dependent; preserve report times and test leakage.

rows.Potential signal: Observed starting/backup role and actual participation could inform a matchup feature when multiple starters are unavailable.
rows.Required observations: Dated depth-chart evidence, active/inactive list, participation/snap counts, position and matchup outcomes. None currently included.
rows.Target / test: Compare against healthy-lineup baseline; test interaction by position group and actual role, not assumed “string” labels.
rows.Known risk / control: Depth labels can be stale or ambiguous; replacements differ in skill and usage. Require dated primary evidence and confidence.

rows.Potential signal: Usage/opportunity counts and role are more directly testable than raw recent output: e.g. targets, carries, routes or participation, where official data is available.
rows.Required observations: Player game statistics, snap/participation data, market line, quote time and settlement definition.
rows.Target / test: Estimate a full outcome distribution; assess calibration and pricing error on out-of-sample props.
rows.Known risk / control: Role volatility, injury-limited participation, selection bias and multiple props. Do not extrapolate a short streak.

rows.Potential signal: Opponent performance split by play type or position could add information only after accounting for opponent quality, pace and opportunities.
rows.Required observations: Official team/player outcomes, stable definitions and sample counts; no split estimates have been produced here.
rows.Target / test: Test feature ablation and calibration versus a simpler opponent-adjusted baseline.
rows.Known risk / control: Small subgroup samples and schedule confounding; shrink unstable estimates and show uncertainty.
rows.Official NFL source: NFL team stats · NFL player stats

rows.Potential signal: Only consider if the independently estimated probability differs enough from a fair, timestamped market probability after uncertainty and costs.
rows.Required observations: Forecast probability, market price(s), market definition, vig handling, timestamp, settlement and stake rules.
rows.Target / test: Evaluate proper scoring, calibration, price improvement and risk-adjusted returns after costs; report uncertainty.
rows.Known risk / control: A single realized result is noisy; never promote based on win/loss or apparent short-run ROI alone.

rows.Potential signal: Do not multiply leg probabilities assuming independence unless independence is tested. Estimate joint outcome probability and compare to a valid combined payout.
rows.Required observations: All component outcomes, same-game context, historical prices/payout rules, leg inclusion/correlation and push/void rules.
rows.Target / test: Compare joint-probability model to independence baseline on held-out combinations; stratify by relationship and game conditions.
rows.Known risk / control: Combinatorial sparsity, selection bias and correlated game scripts. Limit complexity; no combo rewards until dependence validation passes.

rows.Potential signal: Joint props (including teammate or opposing-player combinations) may share volume, pace, score-state or matchup drivers; test rather than assume direction.
rows.Required observations: Joint historical player outcomes, opportunity/participation, contemporaneous lines and exact settlement.
rows.Target / test: Estimate pairwise and conditional dependence with out-of-sample validation; evaluate full combo probability and calibration.
rows.Known risk / control: Raw correlation may hide role, opponent and game-state structure; correlations do not establish causality. Values currently blank.

rows.Proposed signal: Estimate scoring distributions using pregame team performance and availability.
rows.Key dependency: Historical official game data and timestamped lineup inputs.

rows.Proposed signal: Estimate player opportunities and outcomes against opponent context.
rows.Key dependency: Official historical player stats, roles and market lines.

rows.Proposed signal: Model joint outcomes from shared game scenarios instead of multiplying marginal probabilities.
rows.Key dependency: Matched historical outcomes and actual parlay pricing / rules.

rows.Proposed signal: Model correlated player opportunities within the same game.
rows.Key dependency: Player-level joint outcomes, prices and settlement terms.

rows.Requirement: Record source, availability time, retrieval time, rights and version for every input.
rows.Failure condition: Missing, stale, retrospective or unlicensed inputs.

rows.Requirement: Freeze features at prediction time; split chronologically and group related bets by game.
rows.Failure condition: Future information or related outcomes cross folds.

rows.Requirement: Compare against a frozen simple baseline and a timestamped market benchmark where licensed.
Evaluate held-out log loss, Brier score and calibration by market with uncertainty intervals.
rows.Failure condition: Predeclared calibration or sample requirements not met.

rows.Requirement: Backtest fixed stakes with fees, spreads, pushes, voids and available prices.
rows.Failure condition: Results cannot be settled or independently reproduced.

rows.Requirement: Use multiple seasons and game-clustered intervals; correct for multiple strategy searches.
rows.Failure condition: Intervals too wide or evidence disappears in untouched holdout.

rows.Requirement: Freeze rules and score prospective predictions before considering real-money use.

rows.Method / outstanding work: Compute Pearson correlation of settled binary leg outcomes on matched games; report sample count, period and game-clustered uncertainty. Conditional joint probability is needed for pricing.
Estimate win, loss, push and void probabilities from a calibrated predictive distribution; convert conditional win probability to fair odds only under explicit settlement rules.
Rank eligible frozen strategies by predeclared out-of-sample proper score versus baseline; display ROI and uncertainty separately, not just win rate.
Specify eligibility, prize pool, tie rules and minimum sample before launch. No rewards are currently funded.

rows.Required treatment: Stable player identifier; retain display name, team, position, source and observed-at time.
rows.What a source can establish: NFL injury report tables list player and position for entries in the report.
rows.What it cannot establish alone: That a player is absent from a report does not establish full health, active status or participation.

rows.Required treatment: Store report date, status, injury text exactly as published, retrieval time, page URL and correction history.
rows.What a source can establish: NFL reports list injury, practice status and game status for listed players.
rows.What it cannot establish alone: Diagnosis, probability of playing, severity, recovery timeline or expected role must not be inferred.

rows.Required treatment: Keep report game status separate from official inactive / active confirmation and observed participation.
rows.What a source can establish: The report has a “Game Status” field. An explicit status is a report-state observation at a time.
rows.What it cannot establish alone: Questionable is not a quantified probability. “No status shown” must not be converted to active.

rows.Required treatment: Store rank, position group, effective date and evidence source only if a dated source explicitly lists the order.
rows.What a source can establish: NFL team directory provides official team pages, useful starting points for team-published material.
rows.What it cannot establish alone: The directory itself does not prove current first/second/third/fourth string ordering.

rows.Required treatment: Link the absent player to replacement only from dated lineup/depth evidence; distinguish starter, rotational and emergency use.
rows.What a source can establish: Official NFL player/team statistics can support observed game production where published.
rows.What it cannot establish alone: Prior stats alone do not prove who will replace a starter or how they will be used in the next game.

rows.Required treatment: Capture snaps, starts and role by game if a verified, licensed source explicitly supports those fields.
rows.What a source can establish: NFL's stats pages establish an official statistics starting point.
rows.What it cannot establish alone: This implementation has not verified comprehensive snap counts, historical endpoint access or availability rights.

rows.Required treatment: Aggregate confirmed missing players by position group and role, with separate offense and defense views.
rows.What a source can establish: NFL injury reports and player stats can be referenced as starting evidence for listed players and observed outcomes.
rows.What it cannot establish alone: Cannot assume several listed injuries have equal impact or that a named backup is a deficiency without role/quality evidence.

rows.Required treatment: Display source timestamp, age, last update and confidence; mark stale data and suppress affected predictions.
rows.What a source can establish: Official report page is a public source to check at decision time.
rows.What it cannot establish alone: This site has not established an official report API, delivery SLA, or a complete historical snapshot archive.

rows.Pass requirement (proposed): Every feature and price field has an allowed source, license scope, original timestamp and reproducible lineage.
rows.Fail / hold condition: Unknown rights, undocumented scraping, silent transformations or missing provenance → block use.
rows.Evidence needed: Source inventory, terms review, raw snapshots, lineage and change log.

rows.Pass requirement (proposed): Stable event/player IDs, explicit missingness, correction handling and time alignment; no duplicate or impossible values unexplained.
rows.Fail / hold condition: Missing critical price/outcome, stale status, identity mismatch, leakage or untracked correction → suppress forecast.
rows.Evidence needed: Automated schema checks and dated official stat/report snapshots.
rows.Official source: NFL injury report · NFL team stats

rows.Pass requirement (proposed): Forecast is timestamped before the defined market cutoff; only information available at that instant is used.
rows.Fail / hold condition: Any post-cutoff lineup, outcome, revised statistic or future feature in training or evaluation → invalidate run.
rows.Evidence needed: Immutable forecast log, feature timestamps and reproducible chronological split.

rows.Pass requirement (proposed): Freeze hypothesis, feature set, target, benchmark, markets, scoring, filters and stop rules before the holdout.
rows.Fail / hold condition: Repeatedly trying variants on the holdout or changing criteria after results → no promotion.
rows.Evidence needed: Versioned model card and experiment ledger.

rows.Pass requirement (proposed): Beat simple, disclosed baseline out of sample on a proper probability score; check probability calibration by meaningful slices.
rows.Fail / hold condition: Only wins/accuracy/ROI reported, poor calibration, or no benchmark → fail.
rows.Evidence needed: Predicted probabilities, outcome labels, calibration plots and score deltas.

rows.Pass requirement (proposed): Evaluate strictly forward by time, preserve a final untouched period and report uncertainty / resampling method.
rows.Fail / hold condition: Random row split across games/seasons, repeated holdout peeking, or uncertain edge presented as certainty → fail.
rows.Evidence needed: Split timestamps, sample counts, confidence intervals and all market segments tested.

rows.Pass requirement (proposed): Test against a documented timestamped market benchmark with vig, price, limits, latency, push/void and settlement treatment explicit.
rows.Fail / hold condition: No authorized odds history or no reproducible price / settlement → market edge and return are not testable.
rows.Evidence needed: Licensed odds snapshots and settlement definitions; none are in this repo.
rows.Official source: NFL official site (not a verified odds feed)

rows.Pass requirement (proposed): For parlays/prop combos, validate joint probabilities and conditional dependence on held-out combinations; compare to independence baseline.
rows.Fail / hold condition: Multiplying leg probabilities without evidence, sparse combinations, or dependence estimates from test outcomes → fail.
rows.Evidence needed: Joint outcomes, prices, leg definitions and confidence intervals. Current correlations: —.

rows.Pass requirement (proposed): Availability features have dated primary evidence and remain useful in held-out cases; missing or conflicting sources trigger abstention.
rows.Fail / hold condition: Predictions rely on assumed depth order or inferred player availability → fail.
rows.Evidence needed: Report snapshots, verified lineup/replacement evidence and actual participation data.

rows.Pass requirement (proposed): Freeze a version and record forecasts before any reward or user-facing recommendation; monitor freshness and calibration.
rows.Fail / hold condition: Drift, data-source failure, changed market definitions or too few observations → pause / recalibrate.
rows.Evidence needed: Prospective forecast ledger with outcomes and immutable release version.

rows.Pass requirement (proposed): Rank only gate-passing strategies; use a predeclared score that rewards calibration/value and penalizes risk, with uncertainty and minimum activity.
rows.Fail / hold condition: Rewards based on raw win rate, volume-only staking, retrospective selection or unresolved disputes → withhold.
rows.Evidence needed: Published rules, reproducible score, sample eligibility, stake cap, audit trail and conflict process.
rows.Official source: NFL rulebook (official game rules; not reward rules)

rows.Use: Compare stated probabilities with observed frequencies by bins or a reliability curve.
rows.Interpretation boundary: Good calibration alone does not prove a profitable advantage; disclose sample size and uncertainty.

rows.Use: Use Brier score or log loss for probabilistic predictions; predeclare the scoring and handling of rare/extreme probabilities.
rows.Interpretation boundary: Lower score is better for the chosen definition; only compare on identical targets, samples and baselines.

rows.Use: Evaluate only with licensed, timestamped odds and reproducible settlement. Report staking policy and costs.
rows.Interpretation boundary: Neither measure can be computed from NFL performance stats alone. No odds or return values are shown.
rows.Source: NFL official site (not verified odds source)

rows.Use: Show pairwise association and directly validated joint probability for combo strategies.
rows.Interpretation boundary: Correlation is sample- and context-dependent, not a causal claim and not equivalent to a parlay payout probability.

rows.What to do next: Define event/market/settlement schema; review data licenses; secure a permissioned odds-history feed and official outcome sources; build immutable snapshots and validation.
rows.Advantages: Makes price comparison, no-vig benchmarks, timing controls and meaningful backtests possible; supports no-manual-entry automation.
rows.Trade-offs / missing decision: Vendor selection, budget, rights, retained history, books, prop coverage and geo scope remain unknown.
rows.Official source reference: NFL team stats · NFL injury report

rows.What to do next: Build timestamped report ingestion and source history; investigate dated, verifiable lineup/depth and participation evidence; present missing/stale fields rather than guessing.
rows.Advantages: Addresses the user's explicit need to understand missing starters and replacement roles on offense and defense.
rows.Trade-offs / missing decision: Official report does not by itself prove rank, starter identity or expected workload; source and usage rights for deeper participation data must be found.

rows.What to do next: Once A is satisfied, start with a simple pre-registered game-line model and shadow forecasts; pass all validation gates before real recommendations.
rows.Advantages: Limits initial dependence complexity; gives one clean baseline for comparing additional features.
rows.Trade-offs / missing decision: Still needs data, market definition, legal scope, sample threshold and frozen evaluation design.

rows.What to do next: Start immediately with multi-leg combos and leaderboard rewards.
rows.Trade-offs / missing decision: Joint outcomes, price/payout data and correlation are absent; highest risk of implicit independence, combinatorial overfit and confusing luck with skill.
rows.Recommendation: Not recommended now Block until gate 7

columns: What is confirmed / what is not

rows.Question to resolve: Is this private research, a public information product, a betting recommendation service, or a wagering operator?
rows.What is confirmed / what is not: Not established by repository. Applicable legal obligations depend on jurisdiction, distribution, and activity; no legal conclusion is made here.
rows.Discovery action: Record intended users, geographies, monetization, and whether stakes or transactions are ever handled; get qualified legal review.

rows.Question to resolve: Which leagues, seasons, game types, and markets are in scope: spread, total, moneyline, team totals, player props?
rows.What is confirmed / what is not: Only the research goal is known. No market definition, price history, book coverage or settlement rules are in the repo.
rows.Discovery action: Specify market taxonomy, event IDs, kickoff cutoffs, odds format, void/push rules, overtime treatment and accepted books.

rows.Question to resolve: Which source may legally provide/retain historical and real-time odds, props, lineup and play-by-play data?
rows.What is confirmed / what is not: No odds-feed source, contract, API, license or retention rights were found. The NFL stats site is not evidence of odds rights.
rows.Discovery action: Identify candidate providers and obtain written scope, latency, retention, redistribution, derived-data and price-history terms before integration.

rows.Question to resolve: What authoritative source and version will settle each market and label model targets?
rows.What is confirmed / what is not: NFL provides official stats and a rulebook; exact vendor settlement treatment by market is not defined here.
rows.Discovery action: Document outcome source, correction window, player/team identity mapping, market grading and disputed/void handling.

rows.Question to resolve: When do official injury reports become available, and how do we distinguish missing report, healthy, inactive, limited and uncertain?
rows.What is confirmed / what is not: The NFL injury report page includes player, position, injuries, practice status and game status in published tables. Completeness/time snapshots and historical API rights are unverified.
rows.Discovery action: Capture source URL, fetch timestamp, report date, status vocabulary, corrections and blank vs not-listed distinction.

rows.Question to resolve: Who is the next man up, is he second/third/fourth string, and what role / snaps should be expected?
rows.What is confirmed / what is not: Not supplied by repo or established by an injury report alone. NFL team pages and player profiles may identify players but do not establish a current authoritative depth order in this review.
rows.Discovery action: Find dated team-published depth charts or licensed participation data; store the evidence and mark unofficial consensus separately.

rows.Question to resolve: What is the reference price, how is vig removed, and what timestamp represents the actionable market?
rows.What is confirmed / what is not: No prices exist in the repo. Official NFL data pages do not provide a verified odds baseline here.
rows.Discovery action: Choose an eligible price source and book set; preserve raw odds, quote time, limits if licensed, and closing price definition.
rows.Official source: NFL official site (not an odds feed)

rows.Question to resolve: Which outcomes depend on each other within a game or across legs, and under what conditional game script?
rows.What is confirmed / what is not: No historical market/outcome sample or estimated correlation values are present. Values are intentionally blank.
rows.Discovery action: Define paired outcomes and conditional groups; estimate dependence from training data only, with held-out checks and uncertainty intervals.

rows.Question to resolve: What bankroll unit, exposure cap, payout rules, leaderboard score, minimum sample and reward budget apply?
rows.What is confirmed / what is not: No bankroll, reward pool, account model or scoring rule has been set.
rows.Discovery action: Choose transparent, pre-registered risk-adjusted rewards; prohibit credit for unsubmitted/late forecasts and disclose uncertainty.

rows.Question to resolve: How will the system ingest, validate, timestamp, correct and monitor data without manual user entry?
rows.What is confirmed / what is not: No backend, feeds, credentials, scheduler, database, or monitoring is in this repository.
rows.Discovery action: After rights review, design scheduled ingestion, schema, source lineage, freshness checks, alerting, replay and audited correction workflow.

rows.Question to resolve: Will any user account, wagering activity, payment or sensitive data be collected?
rows.What is confirmed / what is not: No accounts or personal data collection exist in this static research site. Future-system scope is unknown.
rows.Discovery action: Minimize personal data, threat-model access, retention and secrets; secure storage and obtain legal/privacy review as applicable.

rows.Question to resolve: What evidence is enough to say a strategy works and merits recognition?
rows.What is confirmed / what is not: No tested strategies or performance observations have been supplied.
rows.Discovery action: Pre-register forecast timing, benchmark, scoring, evaluation windows, uncertainty and minimum evidence before looking at results.

rows.Fact boundary: Inspected NFL report table lists player, position, injuries, practice status and game status. This does not imply depth order, guaranteed availability, or an API/service-level guarantee.

rows.Change to make: Show the capture time on every data table and add a changed-since-capture diff.
rows.Why it improves a decision: In the 12 Nov 2026 verification, 43 of the 151 rows read from the live NFL injury page had changed since the committed 06:32 UTC capture (22 added, 21 practice-status revisions). A reader who cannot see the age of the data can mistake a stale row for a current one.

rows.Change to make: Re-capture the official sources on every deployment, store the SHA-256 of each captured document and print the hash on the source register.
rows.Why it improves a decision: A dated, hashed capture is what makes a snapshot auditable and lets a reviewer prove that a published row came from the official page rather than from memory or from a community mirror.

rows.Change to make: Add a client-side search box and status filter to the injury and depth tables.
rows.Why it improves a decision: The published snapshot holds 254 injury rows and 1,745 depth rows. Without filtering, researching one club's availability or one position group means scrolling the whole league.

rows.Change to make: Add a depth-string view that shows each player's published rank inside the position group, for both units.
rows.Why it improves a decision: The stated need is to know when a second, third or fourth-string player must start. Club charts publish an order inside each position group; the snapshot stores that rank but the site does not yet surface it as a depth string.

rows.Change to make: Build an availability impact matrix that joins injury status to published depth rank and leaves every unconfirmed cell blank.
rows.Why it improves a decision: The injury report and the club depth chart are the two official documents that exist. Joining them answers 'who replaces him, and at what string' without inventing a replacement workload that no source establishes.

rows.Change to make: Show the leaderboard score with its sample size and confidence interval on every strategy row.
rows.Why it improves a decision: A rank without n and an interval is a scoreboard, not evidence. Showing the interval next to the rank is what separates repeatable skill from a short winning streak.

rows.Change to make: Name the failing validation gate on every strategy row instead of a single status word.
rows.Why it improves a decision: A strategy that fails on provenance and a strategy that fails on sample size need completely different work. Naming the gate turns the leaderboard into a task list.

rows.Change to make: Publish a correlation page that lists only empirically measured pairs, each with n and an interval, and prints 'not measurable yet' for every other pair.
rows.Why it improves a decision: Correlation between legs is the input that decides whether a parlay price is real. Publishing an empty matrix with the measurement protocol is safer than publishing a number that cannot be defended.

rows.Change to make: Label every published value with its evidence class: official league, official club, official regulator, methodology authority, secondary or unverified.
rows.Why it improves a decision: The single largest error risk in this repository so far was community data described with official language. A visible evidence class makes that mistake obvious at a glance instead of in an audit.

rows.Change to make: Add a review protocol that records each suggestion as accept, defer or reject with a date and a reason, and show the history on the suggestion row.
rows.Why it improves a decision: The request is to review suggestions and choose a path before implementing. A record of who chose what, and why, is what turns a list of ideas into a decision trail.

rows.Change to make: Add one plain-language line to every page stating what that page can and cannot establish.
rows.Why it improves a decision: Injury designations are report states, not probabilities, and depth order is guidance, not participation. Saying so on the page prevents the most likely misreading before it happens.

rows.Change to make: Keep one canonical register of requirements, questions, suggestions, gates and flags, and generate every page from it.
rows.Why it improves a decision: The repository now holds six workspaces that were written independently. A single generated register stops two pages from stating different facts about the same item.
rows.Status: Partly done — the root pages and the canonical decision lab are generated; the preserved archives still carry their own text.

rows.Change to make: Publish the verified tables as JSON and CSV alongside the HTML.
rows.Why it improves a decision: A machine-readable copy lets another tool consume only the rows that carry an official source, without re-parsing a rendered page.

rows.Finding: The official Week 10 injury report was captured row by row and re-read line by line; 108 of the 108 comparable rows matched exactly.
rows.Evidence: 151 rows transcribed from https://www.nfl.com/injuries/ on 12 Nov 2026 and compared with the committed snapshot field by field.
rows.Consequence for a decision: The published availability table is faithful to the official page as of its capture time.

rows.Finding: The published snapshot is not a historical archive: 43 of the 151 rows read had changed since the 06:32 UTC capture.
rows.Evidence: 22 rows were added (Seattle Seahawks and Cincinnati Bengals gained full tables, plus two new 49ers and one new Cardinals row) and 21 practice designations were revised.
rows.Consequence for a decision: Use the capture time, not today's page, when reasoning about what was known before kickoff. Re-capture before relying on a row.

rows.Finding: Club depth charts publish an order inside each position group, and that order matched the capture exactly.
rows.Evidence: All 60 rows of the Washington Commanders chart matched on unit, position group, published rank and player.
rows.Consequence for a decision: A published rank can be published as published order. It still does not establish a confirmed starter, an assignment or expected snaps.

rows.Finding: No licensed historical odds or player-prop feed is established anywhere in the repository.
rows.Evidence: No provider, contract, API or retention permission for historical prices has been found or recorded.
rows.Consequence for a decision: No independent line can be compared with a market price, so no expected value, correlation between legs or leaderboard score can be computed yet.

rows.Finding: Ten fail-closed gates are defined and none has been passed.
rows.Evidence: Gate G01 requires an official URL, a raw hash and an official outcome confirmation for every record; no record set in this repository satisfies it.
rows.Consequence for a decision: The leaderboard has zero eligible entries by design. Nothing here shows a profitable strategy.

rows.Finding: Fourteen of the twenty-two registered questions are blocking and only two have an answer.
rows.Evidence: Questions Q16 and Q20 are answered from methodology and authority evidence; the rest are open by design and keep a blank answer cell.
rows.Consequence for a decision: Any path that starts with model building before the data-rights and price questions are answered will be measuring noise.

review_protocol.Action: Open the flagged item and its official source link. The link is the starting point for investigation, not a certificate that the answer is there.
Look for the matching question in the questions register. A flag without a registered question is a new item that should be added.
Mark a suggestion as accept, defer or reject with a reason. Implementation starts only after that mark exists.
Open a change request on the repository with the flag ID, the source that closes it and the expected effect on the affected tables.
The next deployment re-captures the official sources and re-runs the verification. The flag stays published until the evidence supports closing it.
